query: PostgreSQL requests are timing out and the connection pool is full. What should I check?
answer: active connections, slow queries, lock waits, pool saturation, database latency, and recent schema or index changes.

sources.title: Database Timeout Runbook
sources.text: # Database Timeout Runbook Database requests can time out when connection pools are exhausted, queries are blocked, indexes are missing, or the database server is under CPU or I/O pressure. Start by checking active connections, slow queries, lock waits, pool saturation, database latency, and recent schema or index changes. For PostgreSQL, inspect pg_stat_activity and long-running queries. Verify that application connection limits align with the database max_connections setting. Mitigation can include terminating pathological queries, increasing pool capacity only when the server has headroom, adding or correcting indexes, reducing transaction duration, and rolling back a recent database change. Avoid blindly increasing timeouts because that can hide an overloaded database and increase resource contention.
